main_library.notes: Reviewed for the released ONNX graph, tensor inventory, recurrent-state ordering, and public deployment license. The upstream license adds deployment restrictions to Apache-2.0; users must review THIRD_PARTY_LICENSE before conversion, distribution, or deployment.

compatibility_reference.notes: Reviewed TEN feature extraction, streaming sample buffering, hysteresis, segment offsets, reset, and flush behavior. VoiceHub does not import or execute sherpa-onnx.

frontend_reference.notes: VoiceHub reproduces the reviewed Librosa-Slaney 40-bin path, 1024-point FFT, pre-emphasis, symmetric 768-sample Hann window, normalization, and three-frame context in differentiable PyTorch. Sherpa fixes the pitch feature to zero for this model.

source_checkpoints.notes: Conversion uses VoiceHub's standard-library protobuf reader. It validates IR 4, opset 9, all graph connections and operator attributes, all 27 source initializers, static input/output namespaces, graph and inventory fingerprints, and an optional caller-supplied SHA-256 before writing Safetensors. ONNX, protobuf, and ONNX Runtime are not imported.

native_checkpoint.notes: The safe artifact stores the complete graph plus frontend mean, inverse standard deviation, Hann window, and mel filters. Inference and fine-tuning need only PyTorch and VoiceHub.

inference: Sherpa-compatible TEN and Silero segment decisions
native Safetensors export and strict reload
training: explicit soft or binary frame labels

numerical_parity.graph_oracle: ONNX Runtime over 25 recurrent random-feature steps
numerical_parity.frontend_oracle: Compiled kaldi-native-fbank 1.22.3 over 10 sequential deterministic 256-sample frames

limitations: TEN does not publish the recipe or dataset used to train the released graph. VoiceHub exposes an explicitly reconstructed masked window-level BCE fine-tuning recipe and does not claim source-training parity.
The reviewed Sherpa compatibility frontend fixes pitch to zero. VoiceHub preserves that behavior for checkpoint parity; changing it would require retraining and a distinct checkpoint format.
No corpus-level accuracy improvement is claimed. The native port preserves the released model numerically; model-quality changes require dataset-specific evaluation.
Differential ONNX checks are development-only oracles. Production and CI runtime paths do not depend on ONNX Runtime.
